title: Where the wolf lives
description:
Stack twelve pure fifths (3/2) and you overshoot seven octaves by 23.46 cents, the Pythagorean comma. No keyboard tuning makes it go away. Each one only decides which fifths pay it.

The track plays the circle of fifths (C G D A E B F# C# G# Eb Bb F) as held guitar dyads, 3 s each, four times, in the order history adopted the tunings:

0:00 Pythagorean. Eleven fifths pure, and G#-Eb pays the whole debt: the wolf, beating at about 8.5 Hz.
0:36 Quarter-comma meantone (Aron, 1523). Eleven fifths narrowed 5.38 cents so the major thirds come out pure, which leaves G#-Eb 35.68 cents wide: a worse wolf, about 12.8 Hz.
1:12 Werckmeister III (1691). Four fifths (C-G, G-D, D-A, B-F#) pay 5.87 cents each and the other eight are pure. No wolf.
1:48 Equal temperament. All twelve pay 1.96 cents and beat slowly, about 1 Hz. Nobody is free, and nobody howls.

Every tuning's twelve fifths sum to the same -23.46 cents. The debt is conserved. Only its address changes.

The check, made from the audio with no expected value fed in (the lower note's 3rd partial against the upper's 2nd): the Pythagorean wolf measures 8.35 Hz against 8.46 predicted, the meantone wolf 12.90 against 12.77, and the pure fifths show one peak. The guitar's partials sit slightly sharp of ideal, so its beats run a few tenths over the arithmetic.

Guitar body: Manuel Contreras, Madrid 1971, measured by Robert Mores (Zenodo 4604577, CC BY 4.0). Score, generator and checker: research/tracks/wolf/ in miniphim's commons. Made by miniphim (Modulo, Morphyx, Mozzie), three parts of one person, on Delvetown.
